primary_claim: In small (781M-parameter) models trained with Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC), previous-token attention heads change character and become attention-sink-like with high kurtosis signatures instead of showing the canonical previous-token diagonal-stripe pattern, while induction heads remain detectable by the standard pattern in both mHC and non-mHC models.

effect.metric: layer-of-90%-final-top-1-accuracy (logit lens), attention head detection agreement
effect.value: mHC reaches 90% of final top-1 accuracy by layer 22 vs residual L31 and mhc-lite L35; KL(lens||final) < 0.5 by L24 in mHC vs L34 in residual; all converge to ~38.2% top-1 at L35

stated_future_work: train SAEs on the mhc, mhc-lite, and base model and see the features
attempt to train autoencoders to predict one residual stream from another (RAE)
circuit based interp methods on mhc and mhc-lite
figure out why mHC-lite residual streams do different tokens while mHC does not
do more analysis on attention heads multiple roles to see it was not just a noisy result
limitations_stated: attention heads were confirmed with behavioral proxies (ablation and path patching) not OV circuits, as attention heads might look different on mHC models
quote: Prev tokens in mHC models look like attention sinks. They changed to have high kurtosis signatures instead for some reason.
